subject: Opstrack discovery: workload sentinel sizing & tokens/sec probe
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Hill <dana.hill@opstrack.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Opstrack discovery: workload sentinel sizing & tokens/sec probe

Thanks again for the call earlier, Dana — good conversation. I wanted to capture the agreements and next steps so we can move to a quick MA (mutual action) probe and sizing handoff to Performance/Ops. High-level recap below: 

- Goal: Validate streaming and batch token velocity to map to a Dedicated or Hosted config with SLOs at 95th pct latency targets.
- Key SLOs you care about: P95 tail < 350ms for streaming low-latency responses; P50 sub-100ms for short text completions. (You confirmed these targets during the call.)
- Workload profile (what you shared): mix of long conversational sessions (~1k tokens/session avg), intermittent short completions (40–120 tokens), and an occasional burst window at end-of-day when batch jobs trigger (~15–20s crest).

Concrete asks / next steps we agreed: 
1) You to share a representative sample CSV of anonymized request metadata (timestamp, tokens_in, tokens_out, model_type, streaming_flag) — we agreed on an initial 48–72 hour slice.
2) Redwood to run a tokens/sec + QPS probe (ma-probe) against a mirror endpoint to measure sustained vs crest throughput and streaming tail under realistic concurrency. Estimated probe duration: 2 hours (baseline) + 30m crest simulation.
3) If probe looks like baseline sustained load with short crests, we’ll propose a slot-sizing recommendation (GPU pool + batching profile + KV cache hints).
4) Interview Ops eng (you suggested Jesse) about retry behavior and client-side timeouts (critical for streaming early-close behavior).

Attachments: I’ve attached a short probe plan and a tiny template for the CSV. Please redacted any PII before sending.

Open questions we flagged: 
- Do your client SDKs open persistent streaming connections for the long sessions or do you re-open per message? That changes concurrency assumptions.
- Do you have percent of sessions that escalate to >2k tokens? We need that to size KV cache persistence vs eviction.

Can you confirm who will send the sample and whether next Tuesday (8/10) works for the probe window? I’ll schedule a 30m sync with Rishi and our performance team once we have the sample.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
(attach: ma-probe-plan-v1.pdf)

From: Dana Hill <dana.hill@opstrack.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: opsflow@opstrack.com
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Opstrack discovery: workload sentinel sizing & tokens/sec probe

Appreciate the clear recap, Marissa — confirming. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- We primarily use persistent streaming connections for chat sessions (mobile/web clients maintain a socket for the session lifetime). Short completions open a new connection.
- Approx distribution: 60% long sessions (avg 900–1,200 tokens), 35% short completions (avg 60 tokens), 5% heavy sessions (>2k tokens). The heavy sessions are symptomatic (support escalations, longer context windows).
- Our peak crest is typically a 10–12 minute window once per day as multiple batch jobs finish and trigger notifications; crest QPS can be 6–8x baseline.

I’ll have Jesse pull the anonymized CSV (48h) and drop into the shared Drive link by EOD Friday. For the probe window, Tuesday 8/10 morning PT works for us — Jesse will be our ops lead for the probe.

Also, we have a compliance constraint: the sample CSV must redact user identifiers and session IDs — we’ll include a mapping key separately for your ops team if needed under an NDA.

-Dana
Head of Platform, Opstrack
(dana.hill@opstrack.com)

Date: Thu, 6 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Opstrack discovery: workload sentinel sizing & tokens/sec probe

Great summary, Marissa — thanks. Couple of engineering checks before we run the probe: 

- Probe target models: please confirm whether you expect us to use an open LLM variant we selected (redwood-3b-int8) as a stand-in, or if you have a custom model you’ll provide. Using a 3B quantized variant gives us a conservative throughput baseline.
- Client parallelism: for streaming, do mobile clients multiplex multiple session streams over one TCP conn or do they serialize? If they multiplex, effective concurrency on the server is higher than connection count.
- Retry/backoff behavior: what are your client retry windows (0 retries vs immediate retry)? Retries can amplify crest behaviour significantly.

Operational note: for the probe we will instrument token/sec, QPS, concurrency, and per-message P95/P99 latency. We’ll also simulate graceful early-close from clients to measure KV cache retention behavior. Expected deliverable: a one-page sizing note (recommended GPU count, batch size profile, expected P95) within 24 hours of probe completion.

If Tuesday morning (8/10) is confirmed, I’ll reserve a probe slot and share the probe URL and a short runbook with Jesse.

- Rishi
Lead Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai)

I attached the probe runbook and the CSV template used on our side for mapping tokens->qps. If anything in the sample looks off, we’ll reconvene for a short 15m sensitive re-scope before running the probe.
